gap: Pāṇini almost never repeats a word. Look at sūtra 6.1.78: the एच् vowels become अय्, अव्, आय्, आव्. But when does that happen? The sūtra doesn't say. Tap the question mark.
flow: The missing word is just upstairs. Sūtra 6.1.77 ends with अचि, when a vowel follows. That word keeps flowing down into the sūtras below it. This is called anuvṛtti. Tap अचि to send it down.
river: अचि flows into twenty-eight later sūtras and then stops, once it is no longer needed. Here is the stretch of chapter six it runs through. Tap any sūtra to see everything it inherits.
headings: Some sūtras are pure headings, called adhikāras. Their words govern a whole block. प्रत्ययः, affix, at 3.1.1 rules over more than eighteen hundred sūtras. Pick a heading to see how far it reaches.
assemble: Now put it all together. Sūtra 3.1.68, कर्तरि शप्, is just two words. Build its full reading step by step: its own words, then inherited words, then the headings above it.
code: If you write code, this will feel familiar. A heading works like a block that sets context, and anuvṛtti is like a value that stays in scope until it is no longer used. The analogy is loose, but it helps.
quiz: One last check, then a summary to keep.
